slot.brief: Circuit diagram of a capacitor network with a battery; ask for the charge on a specific capacitor after series-parallel reduction.

stem: In the circuit shown in the figure, four capacitors C1 = 6 uF, C2 = 3 uF, C3 = 4 uF and C4 = 3 uF are connected to a 12 V battery. The charge on capacitor C1 is

verdicts.working: C₁ and C₂ in series have equivalent capacitance 2 μF; in parallel with C₃, the network is 6 μF. This is in series with C₄, giving total capacitance 2 μF and series charge 24 μC. The parallel network has 4 V across it, so the C₁–C₂ branch carries charge (2 μF)(4 V) = 8 μC.

working:
C1 and C2 are in series: C12 = (6*3)/(6+3) = 2 uF. C12 in parallel with C3 gives Cp = 2 + 4 = 6 uF. Cp in series with C4 gives Ceq = (6*3)/(6+3) = 2 uF. Total charge Q = Ceq*V = 2*12 = 24 uC. This charge passes through C4, so voltage across C4 = Q/C4 = 24/3 = 8 V. Voltage across the parallel group = 12 - 8 = 4 V. Charge on the C1-C2 series branch = C12*4 = 2*4 = 8 uC. Since C1 and C2 are in series, C1 carries 8 uC.

Independent check: C₁ and C₂ in series have equivalent capacitance 2 μF; in parallel with C₃, the network is 6 μF. This is in series with C₄, giving total capacitance 2 μF and series charge 24 μC. The parallel network has 4 V across it, so the C₁–C₂ branch carries charge (2 μF)(4 V) = 8 μC.
solution:
$C_1$ and $C_2$ in series give $C_{12}=\frac{6\times3}{6+3}=2\,\mu\text{F}$; in parallel with $C_3$, this gives $C_p=6\,\mu\text{F}$. In series with $C_4$, $C_{\rm eq}=2\,\mu\text{F}$, so the total charge is $Q=2\times12=24\,\mu\text{C}$.
The voltage across $C_4$ is $24/3=8\,\text{V}$, leaving $4\,\text{V}$ across the parallel network. Thus the charge in the $C_1$–$C_2$ series branch is $Q_{12}=2\times4=8\,\mu\text{C}$; hence $C_1$ carries $8\,\mu\text{C}$.
